Subject: IronGate Labs — Red Team subscription proposal (exec summary + SOW)

Hi Rishi / Marissa —

Thanks for the time on Tuesday. Attached is our proposal and a draft SOW for an annual red-team subscription that covers: external web + API WL (up to 10 assets), internal network assessment (3 segments), and one scenario-based full-scope red team exercise (includes social engineering scope if you opt in). Highlights:

- Subscription model: $75,000 / year (includes two focused retests for critical/high findings); additional retests billed at $2,000 per retest.
- Deliverables: executive summary (suitable for execs), full technical report, vulnerability CSV (CVE, PoC link), prioritized remediation guidance, and one verification retest per critical after fixes.
- Evidence handling: full raw PoCs delivered via encrypted Drive link; sensitive PII redacted in reports by default; we can sign an NDA.
- Insurance & liability: we carry $5M cyber liability; standard liability cap in SOW is $250k (open to negotiation).
- Testing windows: production testing allowed 10pm–4am PT weekdays, and 8pm–6am PT on weekends.

I've attached IronGate_RedTeam_Proposal_20270218.pdf and IRG_SOW_Draft_20270219.docx. If you'd like, we can revise the SOW to include explicit data handling clauses and a tighter liability cap.

Next steps: let me know your redlines and whether you want social engineering in year one (adds $12k). If you confirm, our contracts team will issue a final SOW and a DocuSign link.

Best,
Adam Hussain\Engagement Lead\IronGate Labs

Adam —

Appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifying items from Redwood before we take this to contracts: we want these captured explicitly in the SOW or via a short addendum. Please confirm you can accept or propose language for each:

1) Liability cap: we're asking vendors to accept a cap of $100k for negligence tied to testing that causes direct production downtime. We understand cyber liability exists; need the cap in SOW.
2) Production testing windows: your windows are fine but we need a safety checklist and pre-test playbook (announcement cadence, rollback playbook) and a 72-hour pre-test runbook to be submitted to Ops.
3) Data handling & minimization: any PII found in PoCs must be redacted; vendor must delete raw PII-containing artifacts within 30 days unless we request retention for remediation verification.
4) Evidence delivery: prefer S3 encrypted buckets + presigned URLs over Drive links; confirm support.
5) SLAs for retest turnaround: for critical findings we need verification retests within 10 business days at no extra cost.

Internally looping Laura (security) and Dev (infra) for technical review. Also copied Kar (legal touchpoint) and Marissa (procurement).

If these are acceptable, we'll route to procurement and legal and push for a decision next week.

Thanks,
Rishi\Head of Customer Reliability\Redwood Inference

Laura's technical redlines (summary):
- Pre-test checklist required (signed off by Infra PO) and runbook with rollback steps; vendor must execute a dry-run on a staging environment before hitting prod for any destructive checks.
- No use of customer-supplied credentials unless explicitly authorized. If Golden Ticket or privileged account is required, access will be scoped and provided via short-lived IAM keys and recorded by our audit system.
- Social engineering: we will not permit voice-based phishing without an approved script and legal signoff.
- Evidence format: provide raw PoCs in a passworded ZIP, deliver password out-of-band; deliver a vulnerability CSV aligned to our internal tracker (fields: id, component, CVSS, description, PoC link, remediation owner).
- Post-engagement: vendor to provide remediation assistance (2h advisory) and one free verification retest per critical within 10 business days.

Minor: request that the SOW explicitly excludes any form of data exfiltration testing unless separately approved; clarify the meaning of 'full-scope' in weekly sync notes.

I'll add inline comments to the Word SOW and upload to the shared drive. If we need to loop in legal for contract language on liability, Kar can help.

-Laura
Director, Security Engineering\Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick feedback — this is helpful. Short answers below and next steps:

1) Liability cap: we can accept lowering the operational liability cap to $150k for production-impact events with explicit carveouts for gross negligence; final language to be provided by our contracts team.
2) Production safety checklist & pre-test playbook: yes — we'll deliver a pre-test playbook 72 hours before any prod engagement and follow your rollback checklist. We'll also run the requested staging dry-run.
3) PII handling & deletion: agreed. We'll redact PII in report exports and delete raw PII artifacts from our systems within 30 days unless Redwood requests retention.
4) Evidence delivery: we can deliver via S3 presigned URLs; happy to accept your encryption preferences.
5) SLA for retest: we'll include a 10-business-day verification retest window for critical items at no charge.

Discount: if Redwood signs for the annual subscription and agrees to a 12-month payment term up front, IronGate can offer a 10%first-year discount (net: $67,500). Contracts will prepare a DocuSign with the revised SOW and insurance cert attached.

I'll attach a new SOW with those redlines and include explicit language on access scoping and privileged access controls. Let me know if you want social engineering included — if not, we'll strike that out.

Regards,
Adam Hussain\Engagement Lead\IronGate Labs

Quick operational notes from infra:

- We will only provide short-lived IAM keys (max 24 hours) and temporary privileged sessions via our internal PAM. No static credentials.
- Any golden-ticket style lateral-movement tests must be scoped to an isolated lab network when possible. If a prod privileged path is needed, we require a mutually agreed time window (10pm–4am PT) and a single point of contact from Infra on call.
- We need the vendor to run their initial exploitable PoC against a non-prod duplicate where available. For any test hitting prod stateful systems (payment flows, user sessions), the vendor must provide a detailed step plan 48 hours prior and be prepared to pause at our request.

If IronGate agrees to these operational guardrails, Infra approves moving forward.

-Dev
Staff Site Reliability Engineer\Redwood Inference

Adam —

Thanks for the fast follow-up and the updated SOW (v2). We are aligned on almost all technical points. Two contract items to resolve before we sign:

1) Liability cap: we cannot accept $150k as the sole limit. For production-impact events caused by vendor testing (not gross negligence), Redwood requires a $100k cap. If IronGate accepts, we'll proceed.
2) Payment terms: we prefer Net 30 with a standard purchase order; we will not do full 12-month prepayment. If you can keep the 12-month term but Net 30 payment (invoices quarterly), we'll sign.

If IronGate can accept the two items above, go ahead and issue the final DocuSign for signature and copy Redwood procurement (marissa_cole@redwood.ai). Please also attach your current cyber insurance certificate (we need the carrier, limits, and policy number).

Once we have DocuSign and insurance cert, Procurement + Legal will turn this around quickly.

Rishi\Head of Customer Reliability\Redwood Inference
